newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The presidential palace dismisses claims made by opposition that it was behind covert intelligence surveillance directed at opposition presidential bets, even as a source says the surveillance team has tapped the services of telephone companies to help them in their work. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Senators and lawyers are poised to initiate an impeachment proceeding against election commissioner Manolo Gorospe who is also serving as the corporate secretary of the Armed Forces and Police Savings and Loan Association Inc. (MANILA TIMES)
- The Commission on Elections is prepared to deputise 600,000 public school teachers to man the 200,000 precincts for the elections next year. (BULLETIN)
- Executive Secretary Ruben Torres says the presidential palace wants to see the passage of the comprehensive tax reform bill rather than the amendment to the bank secrecy law. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Treasury bill rates decline across-the-board with tenders swarming the one-year tenor, confirming a downward trending in interest rates. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The Board of Investments will review its policy on imported completely built-up units. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Perfecto Yasay says he wants to grant the Philippine Stock Exchange its self-regulatory licence. (MANILA TIMES)
